messages:
meg: Quick design sync  deciding between inline stacked previews vs a persistent right-hand preview panel for the routing rules editor. QA found keyboard users lose context when multiple previews open.

adir: FWIW I prefer the persistent panel. It avoids layout shift when you open previews repeatedly and makes comparing rules easier. Also we can pin which rule is shown.

taylor: Panel wins for comparison, but it eats horizontal space on small screens. For narrow widths we could auto-float the panel as an overlay that can be dismissed with ESC.

sam: Main accessibility concerns: 1) when panel opens focus should move into the panel (and trap while open), 2) opening a new preview should update content without shifting focus unless user explicitly navigates.

meg: Good points. Alternative hybrid: default to inline stacked previews on wide screens, but open the persistent panel when the user clicks "Compare" or uses a keyboard shortcut. On mobile always use an overlay panel.

adir: Hybrid sounds reasonable. Need rules for focus: if the panel opens via keyboard (Enter/Space on a rule), focus goes to the panel heading; provide a clear "Back to list" button that returns focus to the triggering rule. If opened with mouse, do not trap focus but still make panel focusable.

taylor: Copy for the panel header: show rule title + short status line e.g. "Matches: 2 / 8" and a small action link "Pin". For the inline preview header keep it terse: "Rule preview  Matches: 2".

sam: Validation text discussion: when priorities collide we currently show an ephemeral banner. Proposal: show inline banner on the affected rules and keep the top-of-page banner as a sticky summary with a concise action. Inline copy: "Priority conflict: Rule X and Rule Y both use priority 10." Top banner: "1 priority conflict  Fix".

adir: For the "Fix" action, offer two options: Auto-resolve (increment lower priorities) or Open reorder mode (keyboard-accessible). Make Auto-resolve a clear secondary action.

meg: Simulation notes: the preview panel must reflect timeline playback. When the timeline plays, highlight matching rules in the panel and in the list with a 120ms fade. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Also announcements: use aria-live polite for incremental updates and a final assertive summary if the user clicks "Announce results".

taylor: Reordering UX: when dragging across long lists, the drag ghost should be visually separate from the pinned preview panel so the ghost doesn't get clipped. Proposed ghost style: semi-transparent white with 3px high-contrast outline and a small drop shadow. Keyboard reorder mode should show explicit Move up / Move down buttons with aria-labels.

sam: Small keyboard detail: if the user opens the panel then uses arrow keys to move between rules, update the panel content but do not trap the user. Only trap when the panel is explicitly modal (overlay on mobile or when "Compare" toggles pin).

sim-bot: Scheduling simulation: label="panel-vs-inline-hybrid"  18 runs across widths [360, 768, 1280]. Will test: focus retention, timeline highlight sync, and priority conflict visibility.

adir: Accessibility copy tweaks: change "Expand" to "Show details" and "Collapse" to "Hide details" everywhere. For the inline conflict banner use a succinct sentence: "Priority conflict: Rule A & Rule B share priority 10." Include an inline link "Auto-resolve".

meg: Dev checklist for PR: 1) implement hybrid panel behavior, 2) focus rules (keyboard opens -> focus to heading; back button restores), 3) panel timeline sync + prefer-reduced-motion, 4) inline + top summary validation banners, 5) drag ghost z-index safety. Add unit/e2e tests for focus retention and simulation highlight timing.

sim-bot: Simulation complete  18 runs, 3 failures at width 360 where the panel overlay steals focus and doesn't restore on ESC. Logs: "focusRestoreFailed runs 5, 11, 16".

meg: Thanks. I'll take the ESC/focus restore fix. After that ping sim-bot for a follow-up run. Small PR ok.

sam: I'll update the keyboard docs and add tests for focus restore.

meg: Great work team  we'll include this in the next patch if green.
